quickAnswerTitle: Quick Answer: Comfort Colors vs Gildan, Which Shirt Is Better?
quickAnswer: Comfort Colors is the better choice for a soft, vintage-style tee. Gildan is the better choice for low-cost bulk orders. Comfort Colors 1717 uses heavier ring-spun cotton and garment dyeing. Gildan 5000 costs less and feels stiffer. Pick by budget and by the look you want.
intro: If you want a heavyweight blank t-shirt, you will probably compare comfort colors vs gildan. Both brands belong to Gildan Activewear, but they serve different markets. Comfort Colors aims at a premium, vintage look. Gildan 5000 aims at volume and price. This guide shows the main differences, so you can choose the right shirt for your project.

sections.heading: 1. Fabric and Dyeing: Garment Dye vs Piece Dye
paragraphs: Comfort Colors 1717 is garment dyed. The shirt is sewn from raw cotton first, and then it is dyed. This creates a soft, lived-in look. The color also looks slightly faded around the seams.
Garment dyeing can help reduce shrinkage. Still, always check the size chart before you order.
Gildan 5000 is piece dyed. The fabric is colored in rolls before it is cut and sewn. The color is even and flat. It does not have the faded, vintage feel of Comfort Colors.

sections.heading: 2. Yarn Quality: Ring-Spun vs Carded Cotton
paragraphs: Comfort Colors uses ring-spun cotton. The fibers are spun tighter, so the surface feels smooth. At 6.1 ounces per square yard, the shirt also feels substantial.
Gildan 5000 uses carded cotton, at about 5.3 ounces. Many buyers find it stiffer out of the package. It can also fuzz after several washes.

sections.heading: 3. Fit and Shape: Relaxed Streetwear vs Standard Promo
paragraphs: Comfort Colors 1717 has a relaxed, boxy cut. The collar ribbing stays firm. Many streetwear brands and college merch shops use it for this reason.
Gildan 5000 has a standard fit. It suits everyday wear and printed promo orders. The two brands do not fit the same way, so compare the size charts before you buy.

sections.heading: 4. Price and Order Size
paragraphs: Gildan 5000 usually costs less per shirt. This makes it a strong choice for large promo orders, team shirts and event giveaways.
Comfort Colors costs more because of its heavier fabric and garment dyeing. It suits small runs, boutique brands and gifts where the feel matters most.

sections.heading: 5. Styling Tip: Pair Your Tee with Pants
paragraphs: A washed pepper Comfort Colors tee looks good with tapered utility trousers. It gives a relaxed weekend look without much effort.
For more pant pairings, read our guide to olive green pants and shirt colors.

faqs.question: Why is Comfort Colors more expensive than Gildan?
faqs.answer: Comfort Colors uses heavier ring-spun cotton and garment dyeing. These steps cost more than standard piece dyeing.

faqs.question: Does Comfort Colors shrink in the dryer?
faqs.answer: Garment dyeing helps reduce shrinkage, but results vary. Check the size chart, wash in cold water, and use a low dryer setting.

faqs.question: Is Gildan 5000 good for printing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Gildan 5000 is widely used for screen printing and promo orders because it is affordable and comes in many colors.

faqs.question: Which is softer, Comfort Colors or Gildan?
faqs.answer: Most buyers find Comfort Colors softer because of its ring-spun yarn. Gildan usually feels stiffer until it has been washed several times.
